en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighteenth Chapter
The Discourse on "One Hears Sound": Is it the case that one who has entered [the meditative attainment] hears sound?
Yes, it is.
Having attained [jhāna], he sees forms with the eye …pe… with the ear …pe… with the nose …pe…
“Does one touch a tangible object with the tongue … [and so on] … with the body?
“One should not say so …” etc.
"One who has attained [jhāna] hears a sound"?
Yes. "One who possesses ear-consciousness has attained [jhāna]"? No.
It should not be stated thus.
Is it not the case that concentration belongs to one possessed of mind-consciousness?
Yes, it is.
If concentration belongs to one possessing mind-consciousness, then indeed it should not be said:
"One who has attained meditative absorption hears a sound.
Does concentration belong to one possessing mind-consciousness, while one possessing ear-consciousness hears a sound?
“Yes.
“If concentration belongs to one possessing mind-consciousness, and one possessing ear-consciousness hears a sound, then indeed, it should not be said:
‘One who has attained meditative absorption hears a sound.’”
Is it the case that for one possessing mind-consciousness during meditative absorption (samādhi), one possessing ear-consciousness hears a sound?
Yes. [Does this involve] two contacts? ...pe... [and so on].
"Is there a conjunction of two consciousnesses?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
It should not be said—
“Does one who has attained [the first jhāna] hear sound?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If sound has been called a thorn to the first jhāna by the Blessed One, then indeed, sir, you must say:
‘One who has attained [jhāna] hears sound.’”
It has been said by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna; does one who has attained [the first jhāna] hear sound?
Yes.
It has been said by the Blessed One that applied thought and sustained thought are thorns to the second jhāna; does that [second jhāna] possess applied thought and sustained thought?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Since it was stated by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna, does one who has attained [the first jhāna] hear sound?
Yes.
Rapture is a thorn to the third jhāna...
inhalation and exhalation are a thorn to the fourth jhāna... perception of form is a thorn for one who has attained the base of infinite space...

perception of the base of infinite space is a thorn for one who has attained the base of infinite consciousness... [perception of the base of infinite consciousness is a thorn] for one who has attained the base of nothingness...

For one who has attained the base of infinite consciousness, the perception of the base of infinite consciousness is called a thorn by the Blessed One; for one who has attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the perception of the base of nothingness is called a thorn;
and for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling are called thorns. Does that person still possess perception and feeling?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … The discussion on “he hears a sound” is finished.
